detail.abstract: Although intellectual property laws are deemed an effective tool in promoting innovation in healthcare, their impact on the societal right to cancer research is uncertain. Emerging normative literature demonstrates why the effects of intellectual property rights laws may not be as intended. However, with protection against the entrenchment of intellectual property laws through harnessing the human rights recognized under international and EU laws, States can uphold the benefits of scientific innovations beyond healthcare services. Through a multi-stakeholder collaborative approach, scientists and policymakers can potentially influence the direction of future legislative and policy efforts to align with international and EU human rights standards. This article will explore how cancer research has been reshaped by intellectual property rights laws within the EU and will seek to reconcile the challenges of striking that elusive equilibrium in the public-private interest domain.

title: Mind the (Employment) Gap: The Power of Reasons in Reshaping Employers' Beliefs
affiliations: University of Queensland, School of Economics, University of Queensland and Flinders University

detail.title: Mind the (Employment) Gap: The Power of Reasons in Reshaping Employers' Beliefs
detail.abstract: Using a large vignette-experiment with Australian employers, we show that providing information about employment gaps substantially reshapes employers' beliefs. Absent the reason for the gap, employers' interview intentions are 0.4 standard deviations lower for long-gap candidates (24-26 months) than short-gap candidates (2-4 months), reflecting perceived deficits in motivation and non-cognitive skills. Reasons eliminate two-thirds of this penalty, consistent with Bayesian updating. Caregiving and firm-shutdown reasons benefit long-gap candidates, while injuries harm short-gap candidates and mental-health conditions harm both. These adjustments, which vary based on candidates' gender and age, highlight when information improves hiring prospects and when it backfires.

title: Estimating the Natural Rate of Interest in a Macro-finance Yield Curve Model
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB), De Nederlandsche Bank and European Central Bank

detail.title: Estimating the Natural Rate of Interest in a Macro-finance Yield Curve Model

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: Using a novel macro-finance model we infer jointly the equilibrium real interest rate r*, trend inflation, interest rate expectations, and bond risk premia for the United States. In the model r* plays a dual macro-finance role: as the benchmark real interest rate that closes the output gap and as the time-varying long-run real interest rate that determines the level of the yield curve. Our estimated r* declines over the last decade, with estimation uncertainty being relatively contained. We show that both macro and financial information is important to infer r*. Accounting for the secular decline in interest rates renders term premia more stable than those based on stationary yield curve models. A previous version of this paper by the same authors entitled “Natural rate chimera and bond pricing reality” has been published as ECB Working Paper No 2612.

title: Estimating Treatment Effects with Partially Observed General Confounders
affiliations: University of Chicago and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Estimating Treatment Effects with Partially Observed General Confounders
detail.abstract: Understanding treatment effects is crucial across a wide range of decision-making processes, including medical treatments, policy evaluation, and program assessment. Estimating the average treatment effect from observational data becomes particularly challenging in the presence of unobserved confounders. In this work, we propose a model designed to estimate causal effects using observational data where the confounder is only partially observable. Unlike existing approaches, we relax restrictive assumptions by allowing observability to be correlated with both the treatment and the confounder. We develop a maximum likelihood estimator model to estimate the causal effect under partial observability and prove the model's identifiability. Additionally, we derive the optimal solution for the parameters of interest and establish an (ϵ, δ) concentration bound for the average treatment effect. To validate our analytical results, we conduct numerical experiments using the PharmGKB Warfarin dataset and show that the model is able to accurately recover the true parameters.

title: The Dual of Law: Adversarial Justice as Lagrangian Structure
affiliations: University of Helsinki

detail.title: The Dual of Law: Adversarial Justice as Lagrangian Structure

keywords: Operations Research / Analytical Model of Law

detail.abstract: Legal disputes can be formalized as constrained optimization problems: a party seeks its best feasible outcome subject to statutory, precedential, and constitutional constraints. This Article shows how the adversarial system-plaintiff, defense, and judge-corresponds structurally to the primal-dual framework of convex optimization. The moving party solves a primal program; the responding party plays the dual; the judge selects a saddle point. Under standard regularity assumptions, the values coincide and the duality gap characterizes the available settlement range. Even without convexity, weak duality yields upper and lower bounds on rational bargaining outcomes. The result reframes core features of litigation-settlement, discovery, frivolous suits, plea bargaining, and judicial reasoning-as consequences of a single mathematical structure rather than as isolated procedural doctrines.

title: Does Market Fragmentation Improve Price Efficiency?
affiliations: University of Utah - David Eccles School of Business,  and University of Utah - David Eccles School of Business

detail.title: Does Market Fragmentation Improve Price Efficiency?
detail.abstract: Chen and Duffie (2021) argue that market fragmentation can improve price efficiency by enabling traders to split their orders across venues, reducing their overall price impact, making their trading more aggressive. Testing this theory in equity markets is difficult due to regulatory requirements that distort market independence. The cryptocurrency marketplace provides an ideal setting given its lack of regulatory interference. Taking advantage of sudden and unexpected changes in coin listings, we use a difference-indifference identification strategy to show that fragmentation improves price efficiency, consistent with Chen and Duffie (2021). The implications for the role of fragmentation are essential for improving market quality and investor welfare.

title: Computing Injury Probability from Microscopic Traffic Data: An Energy-Oriented Approach
affiliations: Lund University, Harbin Institute of Technology, Lund University, Harbin Institute of Technology and Lund University

detail.title: Computing Injury Probability from Microscopic Traffic Data: An Energy-Oriented Approach
detail.abstract: Estimating injury risk at traffic sites is a critical component of proactive road safety analysis. Existing methodologies primarily rely on crash-based models, which require large datasets aggregated across multiple sites and extended time periods. These models often fail to incorporate the most influential heterogeneity: impact energy, because precise impact speed is rarely available in crash databases. Instead, segment-level proxies such as posted speed limits or average travel speeds are used, limiting the accuracy and transferability of injury severity predictions. Injury severity models that include impact energy as a predictor also face challenges, as they depend on observed crashes and lack a mechanism to define hypothetical crash events at specific sites.,To address this gap, we propose a hybrid approach that combines the flexibility of Surrogate Measure of Safety (SMoS) and the objectivity of injury severity model to estimate site-specific injury risk without relying on historical crashes. In the approach, SMoS is used to define hypothetical crash events and the energy released during such events, which is interpreted as the distribution of crash severity. The crash severity distribution is extrapolated through bivariate extreme value theory. ,The framework is tested on a Chinese and a Swedish intersection (both signalized). Interaction between turning cars and crossing VRUs are studied. Our findings demonstrate that the site-specific probability of injury is primarily influenced by the distribution of crash severity, which is determined by the joint behavior of proximal and speed related SMoS in near-mises, rather than the crash frequency itself. This supports Safe System approach, emphasizing kinetic energy management over crash frequency.,Moreover, two methodological variations, the Bivariate Peak Over Threshold (BPOT) and Conditional Bivariate Peak Over Threshold (CBPOT) approaches, are compared to assess their suitability for predicting crash severity distribution. We conclude that CBPOT is methodologically more advanced than BPOT in modeling interactions defined by multiple SMoS indicators.,This study makes two key contributions to traffic safety. First, it introduces a mixed approach that enables rapid, scalable evaluation of injury risk at microscopic levels, supporting proactive safety assessment aligned with Vision Zero principle. Second, it summarizes a theoretical framework for modeling multivariate SMoS based on previous studies, which provide practical guidance for implementation and addressing technical challenges.

title: When One Dollar Becomes Two-How Stablecoins Multiply Liquidity Outside the Banking System
affiliations: Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: When One Dollar Becomes Two-How Stablecoins Multiply Liquidity Outside the Banking System
detail.abstract: Fiat-backed stablecoins have become an important part of modern financial markets, yet their monetary effects remain underappreciated. This paper shows that when users convert bank deposits into stablecoins, issuers reinvest the underlying funds in Treasury bills or bank deposits, recreating deposits inside the banking system while the stablecoins circulate outside it. This balance-sheet structure produces a "shadow M2 multiplier," allowing a single pool of base money to support multiple spendable claims. We explain the mechanics behind this effect, contrast stablecoins with tokenized deposits, and analyze the implications for deposit flows, seigniorage, funding markets, and monetary transmission. We also consider how regulatory frameworks such as the GENIUS Act and MiCA shape these dynamics. Finally, we outline a hypothetical scenario in which the U.S. Treasury could obtain spendable stablecoins through its own debt issuance, illustrating how stablecoin architecture could alter traditional fiscal-monetary interactions.

title: Tax-Exemption and the Shadow of Law
affiliations: Yale University - Law School

detail.title: Tax-Exemption and the Shadow of Law
detail.abstract:
President Trump’s recent statements calling for Harvard University’s tax-exempt status to be revoked have sparked considerable debate over whether the IRS can lawfully undertake such an action. Many have assumed that if the government decides to act, it will rely on the “public policy doctrine” from Bob Jones University v. United States. On that basis, most have concluded that the case for revoking Harvard’s exemption is weak. This paper challenges the prevailing narrative by arguing that the IRS has long possessed an alternative legal basis for revoking Harvard’s exempt status. Known as the illegality doctrine, this extra-textual reading of § 501(c)(3) has deep historical roots and operates as a broader and much more powerful tool for enforcing federal tax law. Drawing upon previously overlooked judicial and administrative records, this paper traces the history of the illegality doctrine and reveals how it emerged from decades of administrative improvisation, institutional politics, and ideological policing during the Cold War.

Despite scholarly assumptions that institutional caution substantially limits the potential for abuse, this history demonstrates that the illegality doctrine has remained consistently broad, discretionary, and vulnerable to political manipulation. Tracing its evolution from early judicial skepticism, through Supreme Court validation in Bob Jones, to recent expansions by lower courts, this paper argues that the illegality doctrine is the tax law equivalent of Justice Robert Jackson’s “loaded weapon.” Though it presents a neutral posture and appears grounded in the rule of law, the doctrine is dangerously malleable and insufficiently constrained by statutory clarity or judicial oversight. Ultimately, this paper contends that courts should not overrule Bob Jones but instead cabin it to its narrow core: racial discrimination in education, where bipartisan consensus and explicit statutory mandates converge. Courts should repudiate the broader illegality doctrine as an unauthorized gloss on § 501(c)(3). By limiting Bob Jones to its facts and rejecting illegality outright, courts can preserve the moral clarity of the former while restoring statutory fidelity, democratic accountability, and institutional stability to the law of charitable exemption.

title: Understanding Dairy Industry Innovation Ecosystem: Actor-Role Mapping and Systemic Problems in Indonesia
affiliations: Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management, Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management, Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management and National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN)

detail.title: Understanding Dairy Industry Innovation Ecosystem: Actor-Role Mapping and Systemic Problems in Indonesia
detail.abstract: This study examines the Indonesian dairy industry through the lens of innovation ecosystems, focusing on actor-role mapping and systemic problems undermining innovation and sustainability. Indonesia currently meets less than 21% of its domestic milk demand, indicating a critical gap in local capacity and governance. Using a qualitative research design, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers and staff from two key dairy cooperatives in Java, supplemented by secondary sources, including government policy reports and academic literature. The analysis was conducted using Gioia’s methodology, combining inductive coding with deductive reasoning through an abductive approach. Findings reveal that key actors, including smallholder farmers, cooperatives, processors, NGOs, finance institutions, and government agencies, operate in silos, with minimal synergy or institutional integration. Critical challenges include limited value-added processing (less than 1% of raw milk), feed scarcity, inadequate downstream infrastructure, inactive cooperative associations (e.g., GKSI), uncoordinated public support, and short-term interventions by NGOs. The study concludes that institutional realignment, long-term policy frameworks, and actor coordination are crucial for building a resilient and inclusive innovation ecosystem that supports sustainable dairy development in Indonesia. These findings offer practical insights for enhancing governance, food security, and sustainability in the agricultural sectors of emerging economies.

detail.abstract: The internet has become a key tool for nonprofit transparency, especially in contexts where formal regulatory oversight is weak. This paper explores how nonprofit associations in Lebanon use their websites to communicate transparency and demonstrate accountability. Through an exploratory content analysis of 196 active websites, the study assesses whether Lebanese associations disclose information about their mission, governance, finances, and stakeholder engagement. The results show that while most associations provide basic descriptive details and maintain online communication channels, they rarely publish financial statements, governance documents, or performance reviews. This limited online transparency reflects both structural constraints, like an outdated legal framework and fragmented donor requirements, and organizational choices. The paper underscores the implications of these gaps and offers recommendations to enhance digital transparency and strengthen accountability practices among Lebanese NGOs.

title: Behavioral Insights for Macau's Volatile Real Estate Investment: A Qualitative Approach

detail.title: Behavioral Insights for Macau's Volatile Real Estate Investment: A Qualitative Approach
detail.abstract:
This qualitative phenomenological study examines how real estate professionals in Macau make investment decisions during periods of economic volatility. The gaming-dependent nature of Macau’s property sector creates investment challenges underexplored in existing studies. Through semi-structured interviews with 18 real estate professionals averaging 13.2 years of industry experience, this research explores cognitive processes, behavioral factors, and contextual influences shaping investment choices in Macau's distinctive market environment. Analysis revealed sophisticated adaptation mechanisms, including gaming-tourism dependency creating market hypersensitivity, systematic recalibration of risk parameters, contrarian opportunity identification strategies, and policy-driven risk perception shifts. Findings demonstrate how economic uncertainty fundamentally alters strategic consideration through adaptive decision frameworks, collaborative decision recalibration, and strategic flexibility premium approaches. Investment evaluation during unpredictability is influenced by integrated risk-opportunity assessment frameworks, contextual intelligence networks, experiential pattern recognition, and adaptation-capacity evaluation. These findings extend prospect theory and behavioral decision theory by illustrating how professionals institutionalize cognitive biases into deliberate strategies while developing specialized frameworks for Macau's volatile market conditions. Results provide valuable insights for investment professionals navigating specialized economic contexts and contribute to both theoretical understanding and practical application in property investment during economic uncertainty.

title: Examining Effects of New Pricing Option on Shared Micromobility Use in the Living Lab of Davis, California
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Examining Effects of New Pricing Option on Shared Micromobility Use in the Living Lab of Davis, California
detail.abstract: Shared micromobility (SMM) provides key first and last mile connections but is cost-prohibitive for many users. This study examined the effect of introducing a flat rate pricing option on SPIN usage in Davis, CA, assessing both stated and revealed preferences. First, using the UC Davis Campus Travel Survey, we analyzed a series of choice sets featuring different pricing options and flat rate costs using a multilevel multinomial logistic regression model. Our stated preference results indicated the flat rate was the preferred pricing option for current SPIN users. Then in partnership with SPIN, we conducted a randomized controlled trial of current users in which treatment groups were offered flat rate options with varied costs and duration caps. We investigated pre- and post-intervention SPIN usage with a difference-in-difference model. Revealed preference results showed no change in usage for most treatment groups, with one treatment group exhibiting a slight increase and another a slight decrease. This was likely due to low uptake of the flat rate option and low frequency of SPIN usage overall, meaning a few users could have outsize leverage on results. Further, experimental trial participants did not choose the lowest cost pricing plan for most trips. While results were mixed, this study yields useful lessons related to SMM pricing and design of pricing trials. Communication of incentives could encourage deviation from default pricing structures; associated duration caps may influence uptake of flat rates; and experimental trials may require a longer timeline to observe behavior change given infrequent usage.

detail.abstract: Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) exemplifies the existential crisis facing competition law regarding its purpose, particularly whether it should pursue non-market objectives such as fairness, sustainability, or the democratic functioning of society. Consequently, there is a pressing need to provide a coherent explanation of the seemingly erratic doctrine and jurisprudence on Article 102TFEU and to distil these into a redefinition of such provision. This redefinition should begrounded in economic and comparative reflections on its objectives, enabling the development of a legally and economically robust analytical framework for its future application. Such a framework should address both exclusionary and exploitative abuses and align Article 102 TFEU with the prohibition of agreements and concerted practices under Article 101 TFEU, as well as with the logic of merger control. It also necessitates distinguishing Article 102 TFEU from adjacent regulation, notably Regulation 2022/1925on contestable and fair markets in the digital sector (the Digital Markets Act).

title: Opening the GATE to the Narrow Corridor: A Conceptual Framework for State-Society Balance
affiliations: University of Toronto and University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada

detail.title: Opening the GATE to the Narrow Corridor: A Conceptual Framework for State-Society Balance
detail.abstract: This article examines how societies caught between authoritarian repression and political disorder might enter the "narrow corridor" described by Acemoğlu and Robinson [1]. In this framework, liberty and long-run prosperity emerge when a capable state is constrained by an equally capable society through "inclusive institutions" [2]. We adopt this recipe and distinguish between the government side-rulers, bureaucrats, and oligarchic networks-and the societal side of citizens and their independent institutions. Drawing on the case of Iran, and maintaining a critical perspective toward the authoritarian Islamic regime in Iran, we argue that repeated repression and unfulfilled promises have eroded social capital and generated deep mistrust, hindering citizens' willingness to delegate authority to any new centralized leadership. To address this challenge, we propose a conceptual framework-the Governance-Accountability and Trust Engine (GATE)-which utilizes institution-level elections, transparent performance metrics, and modern information technologies to strengthen democratic practice and rebalance power, once the willingness exists. Rather than offering a fixed constitutional design, GATE outlines an institution-centered pathway through which fragile states may gradually approach the narrow corridor.

title: A Study on factors influencing users’ willingness to adopt generative AI-provided travel information based on SEM and FSQCA

detail.title: A Study on factors influencing users’ willingness to adopt generative AI-provided travel information based on SEM and FSQCA
detail.abstract: This study focuses on users’ behavioural willingness to adopt tourism information provided by generative artificial intelligence, aiming to identify key factors influencing this willingness and to delve into its underlying mechanisms. User data collected through semi-structured interviews, combined with grounded theory methodology, distilled core categories including information quality, source credibility, and perceived risk. Findings reveal that users undergo a dynamic cognitive-affective-behavioural evolution when adopting AI-generated tourism information: enhanced information quality and source credibility increase perceived attractiveness and reduce perceived risk, thereby strengthening adoption intent. The negative impact of perceived risk is mitigated under high information quality and source credibility conditions. Furthermore, users’ behavioural outcomes feed back to influence subsequent cognitive evaluations and affective responses, forming a cyclical dynamic process. The model constructed in this study reveals the complex influence mechanisms underlying the adoption of generative AI-generated tourism information. It provides theoretical foundations and practical pathways for tourism information service providers to design algorithm transparency enhancement strategies and establish ethical risk prevention and control systems.

title: Post-Colonial West Bengal, From Prosperity to Decline: A Brief Analysis of the Possible Causes of Decline

detail.title: Post-Colonial West Bengal, From Prosperity to Decline: A Brief Analysis of the Possible Causes of Decline
detail.abstract: Before the British East India Company invaded Bengal in 1757, it was one of the richest areas of the Asian subcontinent. However, it has repeatedly been the target of political and economic hostility both throughout the British and post-independence periods. West Bengal led all Indian states in industrial contribution even after the country was divided, continuing to do so until the early 1950s. Then the downturn began. This paper discusses the various causes of the decline. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data on Credit-Deposit Ratio of post-independent Bengal compared to other states gives us some alarming conclusions on how the savings of West Bengal have been siphoned out of the state! The possible historical causes of Bengal's economic decline during the post-colonial phase have been identified from existing literature. A sample survey has been conducted on business leaders and academia, with a structured questionnaire, to understand their perception of the possible causes of decline. We have arrived at fourteen factors that clearly indicate the political and socio-cultural reasons, which are considered important by the respondents of the survey, for the decline of Bengal's industry during seven decades of independence.

detail.abstract: In her Opinion of 19 June 2025 in Case C‑738/22 P Google LLC, Alphabet Inc. v European Commission (the ‘Opinion’), Advocate General Kokott reluctantly takes a decisive step in the direction of recognising at least two important aspects of the analytical framework for exclusionary abuses. Recent case law leaves little room for deciding otherwise, which she uses to sow seeds of doubt that need to be addressed here to avoid any misunderstandings. On the one hand, she implicitly acknowledges the (limited) role of counterfactual analysis under Article 102 TFEU as a method of delineating the content of the conduct in question. On the other hand, she follows a winding path to recognise the capability of excluding a hypothetical equally efficient competitor as the generally applicable benchmark for finding an exclusionary abuse.

title: Malware Family Classification using Adaptive Multimodal Fusion and Modality-Aware Feature Selection
affiliations: Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University and Northeast Electric Power University

detail.title: Malware Family Classification using Adaptive Multimodal Fusion and Modality-Aware Feature Selection
detail.abstract: The increasingly rampant spread of malware, coupled with the rapid evolution of its variants and imbalanced family distribution, has posed severe threats to the reliability of digital infrastructures worldwide.To this end, we propose an adaptive multimodal learning framework, whose novelty lies in integrating byte-level features, structural features, and semantic representations of malware to achieve robust family classification.The proposed multimodal learning framework captures the encoding characteristics of the byte modality through normalized byte histograms and local entropy distributions. In the structural modality, it constructs control flow graphs (CFG) and API call graphs (ACG) to capture program execution logic and system call behavior. In the semantic modality, the framework integrates the TFIDF weighting strategy with ASM2VEC embedding to extract opcode-level semantic representations.To reduce multimodal feature redundancy and alleviate modality heterogeneity, we propose a Modality-Aware Feature Selection (MAFS) mechanism that employs tree-based importance ranking combined with dynamic Top-K filtering for key feature extraction. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive fusion strategy that dynamically selects ensemble learning methods based on modality availability, thereby enhancing the model’s robustness against feature missingness and imbalanced family distributions.Experimental results on a malware dataset comprising 5,841 samples across ten families demonstrate that our model achieves 99.87% accuracy, 99.82% macro-average F1-score, and a log-loss of merely 0.0175. These results validate the superiority of our approach and provide an effective new pathway for malware variant identification.

title: Closing Multiple Sanction Loopholes
affiliations: Max Planck Institute for Tax Law and Public Finance and Dresden University of Technology - Faculty of Economics and Business Management

detail.title: Closing Multiple Sanction Loopholes

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The enforcement of international sanctions is frequently undermined by multiple third-party sanction-breaking countries. This paper examines how a sanctioning country can optimally negotiate with several such loophole countries to close the enforcement gaps. We compare several sequential and simultaneous bargaining strategies. Suitably chosen sequencing, but also simultaneous negotiations under the Single-Undertaking Principle can minimize the cost to the sanctioning country by creating competitive pressure among the loophole countries. We find that, if the desire to make the sanctioning regime effective is sufficiently high, the ultimate goal of closing the sanction loopholes is achieved for all sequencing rules of ultimatum bargaining we consider. However, the equilibrium size and distribution of compensation among loophole countries differ. We characterize the optimal sequential strategy and the optimal simultaneous-offer strategy. Furthermore, for well-chosen negotiation strategies, the sum of compensations paid to multiple loophole countries is lower than if there is only one loophole country.

title: SCADI: A GNN and Knowledge Graph-based Causal Discovery Framework for Cyber Attacks Prediction
affiliations: Mohammed V University of Rabat National School of Computer Science and Systems Analysis and Mohammed V University of Rabat National School of Computer Science and Systems Analysis

detail.title: SCADI: A GNN and Knowledge Graph-based Causal Discovery Framework for Cyber Attacks Prediction
detail.abstract: Understanding causal relationships in the field of cyber threat intelligence is crucial for anticipating the evolution of attacks and designing effective defense mechanisms. This work proposes the SCADI (Semantic Causal Attack Discovery Intelligence) Framework. This causal discovery system considers semantic aspects, intended to infer and validate links between attack patterns and their consequences. Based on the CAPEC and CWE knowledge base, the framework encodes structural and semantic attributes within enriched node representations, integrates modeling of attack progression, and uses a hybrid, multi-scale graph neural network to predict causal links. Monte Carlo dropout is incorporated to account for uncertainty, allowing for the cautious identification of new causal relationships. According to experiments conducted on CAPEC and CWE data, the framework achieves an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.975 and an average accuracy of 0.946, outperforming benchmark methods such as PC, GES, LiNGAM, and NOTEARS. The system can enhance threat intelligence databases by reliably identifying new connections and accurately reconstructing existing ones. These results show the value of combining semantic modeling and probabilistic reasoning for causal discovery in the cybersecurity domain.

detail.title: Integrating HR Innovation Capacity and Community Empowerment for Sustainable Heritage Tourism: The Kajoetangan Model from Indonesia
detail.abstract: Background: The management of community-based cultural heritage tourism in Indonesia still faces challenges in integrating technological innovation with human and sustainability aspects. Kampung Heritage Kajoetangan in Malang City offers a unique opportunity to explore a sustainable Human Resource (HR) management model. Objective: This study aims to analyze and describe three important pillars in HR management: Innovation Absorption Capacity, Community Empowerment, and their impact on Sustainable Development. Method: A descriptive qualitative method with a case study approach was used to collect data from various sources, including Pokdarwis, neighborhood managers, the City Government, and MSME actors. Results: The findings show that Kampung Kajoetangan has successfully integrated technological innovation through digital skills training, empowered the community through active involvement in decision-making, and implemented environmentally friendly practices. Conclusion: The synergy model between Pokdarwis and local initiatives provides balanced social, economic, and environmental benefits and offers insights that can be adapted by similar tourism destinations in other countries to achieve inclusive and sustainable tourism in the digital era.

title: The Architecture of Amplified Perception: Introducing Perceived Exaggerated Amplification (P-E-A)

detail.title: The Architecture of Amplified Perception: Introducing Perceived Exaggerated Amplification (P-E-A)
detail.abstract: In their early years, social media platforms promised safe spaces for diverse opinions and respectful discussion. In reality, users often encounter feeds dominated by extreme perspectives and interact mainly with like-minded peers, reinforcing existing beliefs sometimes fivefold, as research shows. Existing concepts such as echo chambers, filter bubbles, and pluralistic ignorance partially explain this phenomenon, but they fail to capture the inflation and distortion of in-group consensus and the digital-age mechanisms that exaggerate extreme opinions beyond their real-world prevalence. This paper introduces Perceived Exaggerated Amplification (P-E-A), a measurable, interdisciplinary framework that quantifies how algorithmic systems amplify perceived prevalence and intensity of extreme opinions, offering insights for social media design, ethics, and understanding digital perception.

detail.abstract: The literature on multivariate time series is, largely, limited to either models based on the multivariate Gaussian distribution or models specifically developed for a given application. In this paper we develop a general approach which is based on an underlying, unobserved, Gaussian Vector Autoregressive (VAR) model. Using a transformation, we can capture the time dynamics as well as the distributional properties of a multivariate time series. The model is called the Vector AutoRegressive To Anyting (VARTA) model and was originally presented by Biller and Nelson (2003) who used it for the purpose of simulation. In this paper we derive a maximum likelihood estimator for the model and investigate its performance. We also provide diagnostic analysis and how to compute the predictive distribution. The proposed approach can provide better estimates about the forecasting distributions which can be of every kind not necessarily Gaussian distributions as for the standard VAR models.

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Discrimination in Sports Team Selection: Ethical Challenges and Solutions
detail.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in sports team selection processes presents both significant opportunities and pressing ethical concerns. While AIdriven tools have the potential to enhance objectivity and efficiency in evaluating athletes, evidence indicates that they may propagate—or even amplify—pre-existing biases related to race, gender, and physical attributes. This study addresses the urgent need to identify and mitigate discriminatory risks associated with AI-based decision-making in sports. The research aims to evaluate the extent and forms of AI-induced bias in team selection, employing a mixed-methods design: quantitative analysis of selection outcomes via logistic regression and qualitative think-aloud cognitive interviews with scouts. Findings reveal that the use of anonymized player data through AI “blind scouting” significantly reduces attention to non-performance characteristics, shifting focus toward tactical skills and strategic decision-making. Nevertheless, latent algorithmic and data-driven biases persist, underscoring the importance of transparent model governance and ongoing human oversight. The study concludes that collaboration between AI systems and human experts—guided by robust ethical frameworks—offers a path to more equitable and accountable team selection practices. Novel contributions include a hybrid evaluation protocol and a practical set of ethical guidelines for sports organizations. This work advances the discourse on fair AI application in high-stakes environments while providing actionable solutions tailored for sports management stakeholders.

detail.title: Computing Students' Attitudes Toward ChatGPT Across Learning Modalities in Programming Courses
detail.abstract: This study aims to explore computing students' attitudes toward ChatGPT across online, faceto-face (F2F), and hybrid learning modalities in programming courses. It also examines how key factors such as task complexity, self-efficacy, AI literacy, outcome expectations, and dependency vary across these learning environments using descriptive cross-sectional research design. Students generally perceive ChatGPT positively in online programming tasks, valuing its usefulness and ability to enhance skills, though they acknowledge challenges related to task complexity, usability, and over-reliance, with high expectations for its role in complementing learning while maintaining strong self-efficacy and AI literacy. Significant differences among learning modality groups in attitudes toward ChatGPT and perceptions of task complexity was observed, while no significant differences were found for self-efficacy, AI literacy, outcome expectations, or dependency, indicating that these factors remain consistent across groups. Recommendations are discussed.

detail.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Choose a Research Topic: A Comparative Study of Tax Evasion in Turkey and Greece
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in academic research by detailing how Grok, an AI assistant, was used to select a comparative study on attitudes toward tax evasion in Turkey and Greece. The authors queried Grok for Turkey's bordering countries and recommendations for comparison, leading to the selection of Greece due to shared geographic, cultural, and economic factors. However, Grok's cited data on tax morale from the World Values Survey (WVS) proved inaccurate-potentially an AI hallucination or outdated information-highlighting the need for verification. A literature review synthesizes studies on tax evasion drivers in both countries, including institutional, cultural, and demographic influences. Using WVS Wave 7 data (2017-2022) from 1,193 Greek and 2,395 Turkish respondents, the empirical analysis employs Welch's t-tests to compare views on whether tax evasion is justifiable (1=never, 10=always). Results show similar strong opposition overall (means: Greece 1.67, Turkey 1.69; p=0.7108). Demographic breakdowns reveal: no gender differences; age significant only for Greeks (older more opposed); education inversely related to opposition in Greece; income inversely related in Turkey. The study underscores AI's utility and limitations in research while contributing to comparative ethics of tax evasion.

detail.abstract:
Although compliance and ethical governance are well-articulated in institutions’ codes of conduct and constitutions, they often remain inefficient and, on the surface, due to the oversight mechanisms may not work efficiently. This research paper first examines and explains core ethical governance pillars and their relationship with compliance while underscoring compliance and the importance of oversight mechanisms.

The articulation of ethical values is not the sole objective of ethical governance; rather, the ultimate goal is to build a working environment where these values are internalized and reflected in every aspect of business conduct. This means that it should not be merely treated and considered a theoretical concept, it should be actively practiced and strategic long-term plans for the corporates. It is apparent that to strive to practice these ethical values, facilitating robust oversight mechanisms is an inevitable requisite. From this perspective, promoting and internalizing ethical principles requires transforming them into measurable indicators through oversight processes while facilitating transparent decision-making systems. In light of this approach, the paper delves into the interplay between oversight mechanisms and ethical or corporate governance, given their vital role in demonstrating how the core principles and rules of governance operate within businesses and in serving as indicators of a corporation’s long-term sustainability goals. However, these procedures should focus on operational processes rather than attempting to measure ethical principles.

The paper further examines how robust and concrete oversight mechanisms can be established within institutions. Finally, it highlights the paramount role of ethical leadership in promoting and internalizing ethical principles within organizations. Whereas there are multiple challenges to navigate and integrate ethical values within corporate governance, given that ethical governance is multifaceted, the only way to build resilient, sustainable business and ensure long-term success is rooted in the integration of strong ethical systems into corporate structures.

The Paper ultimately aims to show a practical and comprehensive frame for the implementation of ethical governance while emphasizing the significance of ethical governance for transformational effects on sustainable development.

title: The Natural Rate of Inflation

detail.title: The Natural Rate of Inflation

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: I identify the natural rate of inflation: the threshold where signal-to-noise crosses unity. Extending Lucas (1972), I show that when inflation falls below sectoral volatility, firms cannot distinguish aggregate from idiosyncratic shocks. Sticky-price firms rationally filter out competitor price movements, creating endogenous stability. When inflation exceeds the natural rate, filtering ceases, coordination increases, and inflation becomes self-reinforcing. Using six million UK micro-price observations, I estimatethis threshold at 1.9%. Crossing it triggers a regime shift: price dispersion falls 10%, inflation persistence jumps from near-zero to 0.44, and monetary policy loses traction. These findings validate 2% targets as the limit of self-correction.

detail.abstract: This article examines the impact of international labor migration and remittances on the economy of Uzbekistan. In particular, it analyzes the effects of migration on household-level socioeconomic welfare, poverty, the education and healthcare systems, and overall stability in the national economy. Based on official statistics, reports from international organizations, and scientific literature, the article provides policy recommendations for regulating migration flows, strengthening financial inclusion through remittances, and protecting the rights of labor migrants. It also discusses the current state of migration research in Uzbekistan, its economic implications, existing challenges, and future directions. Finally, scientific proposals and recommendations are given for ensuring a migration policy that benefits the national economy.

detail.title: The Corporate Reckoning: How AI-Driven Efficiency is Reshaping Human Value Across Modern Corporations
detail.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence has created a managerial paradox: as organizations become more efficient, they risk becoming less human. This conceptual paper extends Displacement Value Theory (DVT) through the Corporate Displacement Framework (CDF)—a model explaining how AI-driven efficiency reshapes organizational legitimacy, employee identity, and cultural cohesion. Drawing from institutional theory, moral economy, and resilience research, the paper theorizes a cascade of economic, identity, and cultural displacement that erodes moral capital and increases organizational fragility. The framework also introduces Value Reintegration Strategies—ethical leadership, human–AI collaboration, and narrative communication—as mechanisms for restoring balance between technological progress and human purpose. By reframing efficiency as a moral variable within business performance, the study bridges ethical theory and managerial practice, offering executives a diagnostic lens for anticipating the social costs of AI transformation and contributing a midrange theory of how efficiency reconfigures moral legitimacy within firms.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of food safety compliance, location, and product variety on the daily income of street food vendors in Talisayan, Misamis Oriental, Philippines. Recognizing the street food sector's vital role in local economies and public health, the research aims to quantify how adherence to safety standards, the strategic quality of the vending site, and the breadth of the menu affect vendors' financial performance in a rural context. A quantitative, correlational research design was employed, utilizing a structured, researcher-made questionnaire to collect numerical data. The target population comprised street food vendors in Talisayan, selected using a simple random sampling technique. The data gathering involved in-person administration of the pilot-tested instrument, followed by the use of descriptive statistics and inferential statistical techniques, specifically correlation analysis and regression modeling, to assess the relationships among the variables. Findings revealed a statistically significant negative relationship between food safety compliance and daily income. This suggests that while essential for public health, compliance may introduce operational costs that negatively impact earnings. Conversely, the location of the vendors demonstrated a statistically significant and positive influence on daily income, highlighting its critical role as a determinant of earnings. In contrast, product variety did not exhibit a statistically significant impact on daily income. Statistical analysis concluded that among the variables examined, only location was a significant predictor of the daily income of street food vendors in Talisayan, Misamis Oriental, leading to the rejection of the hypothesis that all three factors positively influence income. The study concludes that strategic location is the paramount factor for optimizing vendor income, while the costs associated with food safety compliance present a significant challenge to economic sustainability.

detail.title: Influence of Digital Wallets on the Financial Behavior of HEI's Students
detail.abstract: This paper explores the influence of digital wallet usage on the financial behavior of Higher Education Institution (HEI) students in a State University of the Philippines. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research examined determinants of digital wallet adoption, including perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, perceived value, social influence, perceived trust, perceived security, and intention to use. Financial behavior was assessed through cash management and financial planning and budgeting. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, data were collected from 219 randomly selected participants through validated survey instruments. Results revealed that students generally perceived digital wallets positively and exhibited responsible financial practices. Regression analysis confirmed a significant positive effect of digital wallet usage on financial behavior, accounting for 45.4% of the variance. The study concludes that digital wallets contribute to improved financial management among students and recommends integrating digital financial literacy programs into HEIs. Further research should consider diverse populations and explore long-term effects of digital wallet usage.

title: The Primary-Source Vacuum: How the Post-1945 Omission of Five Perpetrator-Generated Document Clusters Created the Enabling Conditions for Contemporary Revisionist Narratives

detail.title: The Primary-Source Vacuum: How the Post-1945 Omission of Five Perpetrator-Generated Document Clusters Created the Enabling Conditions for Contemporary Revisionist Narratives
detail.abstract: This study demonstrates that five clusters of official Reich statistics and perpetrator-authored texts (1919-1943) were systematically excluded or radically condensed in Western post-1945 secondary-school and introductory university curricula. When these identical primary sources are later encountered without their original criminal context, they generate a coherent revisionist narrative that portrays National Socialism as a legitimate, popular, and programmatically consistent response to post-1918 crises. The resulting explanatory vacuum is a direct, structural consequence of the deliberate pedagogical simplification adopted between 1945 and approximately 1960. The analysis is restricted exclusively to perpetrator-generated documents; no secondary literature, victim testimony, Allied reports, or postwar judicial material is cited.

title: The Nahj al-Balagha’s View of Inequality and Social Classes in Comparison with Karl Marx’s Theory

detail.title: The Nahj al-Balagha’s View of Inequality and Social Classes in Comparison with Karl Marx’s Theory
detail.abstract:
In explaining inequality and social classes, there are different perspectives with different approaches. Marx, as a conflict sociologist, has the greatest contribution in presenting the concept of social class. Given that this phenomenon has been deal with in Nahjul-Balagha, we sought, in this research, to answer the question of whether the concept of class and classes in Nahjul-Balagha is the same as or different from what Marx proposed. In the present study, using content analysis as an inference method, we came to the conclusion that the concept of class and social classes in Nahjul-Balagha, unlike Marx's view, is not based on the means of production and wealth. Rather, it refers to the individuals’ social status and conditions – what the sociologists call “social base”. The common point between Nahjul-Balagha and Marx’s theory is the idea of inequality and social classes. However, there is a difference between them as to what produced inequality and social classes.

title: Economic Crises and the Evolution of Theory: A Methodological Inquiry into Paradigm Shifts and Research Programs

detail.title: Economic Crises and the Evolution of Theory: A Methodological Inquiry into Paradigm Shifts and Research Programs
detail.abstract: Economic crises have historically marked turning points in economic thought, often catalyzing theoretical transformations. This article analyzes how recent crises have exposed the limits of mainstream economics and revisits two major theoretical 'revolutions'-Keynesian and Marxist-framed through the lenses of Kuhn, Popper, and Lakatos. Keynes identified crises as failures in aggregate demand remediable through state intervention, while Marx viewed them as inherent to capitalism's internal contradictions. The paper argues that, unlike natural sciences, economics has resisted definitive paradigm shifts due to ideological entrenchment. Ultimately, it calls for a rethinking of economic theory grounded in heterodox perspectives and attentive to historical and institutional contexts.

title: Burdens or Builders? Housing Market Effects of Afghan Refugees in Iran

detail.title: Burdens or Builders? Housing Market Effects of Afghan Refugees in Iran
detail.abstract: Large refugee inflows expand demand in the host country's housing market, increasing rents for natives when supply is slow to adjust. We revisit the "burden" narrative in a setting where refugees also reduce construction costs by supplying low-cost labor. We study the impact of the approximately three-million-person inflow of Afghan refugees to Iran following the Taliban's 2021 takeover. Employing an instrumental-variables difference-indifferences (IV-DiD) design, we find no significant effects on housing expenditures and, using provincial construction records, present evidence that stronger supply responses in refugee-exposed provinces mitigated upward pressure on housing costs. The theoretical framework we develop formalizes conditions under which opposing demand and supply forces can offset one another.

detail.title: The Grievances of a Failed Reform: Chilean Land Reform and Conflict with Indigenous Communities
detail.abstract: Land reforms are among the most significant institutional changes in developing countries, yet they often fail due to interruptions or reversals. This paper examines the long-term effects of the Chilean land reform (1962-1973) on indigenous selfdetermination conflict. A major redistribution was fully reversed in the study area after the 1973 military coup. Using a novel plot-level database, we show that expropriated plots are over four times more likely to experience invasions and attacks between 1990 and 2021. Instrumental variable estimates, based on rainfall shocks affecting reform participation, confirm these findings. The failed reform produced grievances both within and beyond indigenous reservations, subsequently reactivated by the counter-reform's production structure and by recent restitution policies.

title: From Discrete Choice to Possibility- A New Method for Modelling Fuzzy and Random Uncertainties in Travel Behaviour

detail.title: From Discrete Choice to Possibility- A New Method for Modelling Fuzzy and Random Uncertainties in Travel Behaviour
detail.abstract: This study introduces a novel approach for mode choice modelling based on possibility calculus theory, which addresses both randomness and fuzziness. The Max P-S technique, a fuzzy estimation process, is used to estimate the parameters within the logit model. By comparing the Max P-S technique directly with the conventional logit that uses the maximum likelihood estimation, the impact of the different estimation process is highlighted. The comparative analysis reveals that the Max P-S model consistently and significantly outperforms the MLE-based Logit model across multiple performance metrics. It achieved a substantial increase in predictive accuracy, with up to a 10% improvement on local SIDS models and a 13% increase on a Swiss model. This predictive superiority is substantiated by significantly lower RMSE and MAE values, indicating a more precise alignment with observed choices. Additionally, a lower AIC confirms the Max P-S model's superior efficiency and parsimony. Beyond prediction, the Max P-S technique provides more robust and theoretically sound explanatory power. Wald statistics demonstrated that the Max P-S technique consistently produced highly significant coefficients that align with established theory, unlike the MLE-based Logit model, which occasionally yielded problematic results. Sensitivity analysis further highlights this strength, showcasing the Max P-S technique's ability to capture realistic, non-linear behavioural thresholds and nuanced responses that are often missed by conventional Logit models. These findings underscore the value of flexible frameworks like the Max P-S technique for effective policy design and data analysis in SIDS. Future research can explore applying the Max P-S to other choice modelling techniques.

detail.title: Stress-Testing Machine Learning Models for Stock Forecasting with Minimalist Feature Sets
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of stock market indices is an important part of financial decision making. This study performs a stress test of machine learning models by forecasting the Dow Jones Australia Index (DJ Australia) from 2015 to 2025 using a minimalist set of purely temporal features. Eight regression models; Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression (SVR), XGBoost, Random Forest, k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP), LightGBM, and CatBoost are evaluated in this study under time-series split. Feature engineering here is limited to extracting components (year, month, day, and day of the week) from the date  to create an environment with constrained information for testing model robustness. Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) were used for performance assessment. Contrary to expectations that complex models would perform better on complex data, the stress test results indicated that Linear Regression was the most robust by achieving the lowest error metrics (RMSE: 29.853; MAPE: 7.05%). More advanced modeling techniques such as MLP and SVR have spectacularly failed indicating strong overfitting tendencies without powerful features, a finding which challenges complexity bias default in financial machine learning and highlights baseline model importance in low-information environments.

detail.title: Commodification Technology and Market Commodity Structure: General Equilibrium Approach
detail.abstract: In this paper, we formalize the concept of commodification technology that, within an extended Arrow-Debreu general equilibrium framework, endogenously determines the market commodity structure. In the spirit of Mas-Colell (1975)’s commodity differentiation approach and Rosen (1974)’s hedonic model, commodities are modeled as bundles of characteristics. The quality of each commodity, as well as the market viability problem under asymmetric information arguments such as Dubey et al. (2000) and Bisin et al. (2011) concerning the determination of market structure, is treated uniformly as an endogenous equilibrium state in the strict sense of general equilibrium theory. In our model, each market participant (consumer or a producer) is endowed with a commodification technology that enables the agent to prepare market commodities that agent’s endowments and a transformation technology for basic characteristics, thereby representing the costs for standardization, advertisement, signaling, and related activities. This framework also provides a tractable general equilibrium tool for analyzing the role of potentially redundant markets, the placebo (nocebo) effects, the formation of new futures markets in general equilibrium theory, and platform-based industrial organization and disruptive innovation in management science.

title: A Decision-Making Framework for Human-LLM Collaboration in Smart Grids

detail.title: A Decision-Making Framework for Human-LLM Collaboration in Smart Grids
detail.abstract: Smart grid operations are increasingly complex, requiring human operators to rapidly process heterogeneous information to assess node failures and deploy countermeasures. Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful decision support tools by synthesizing operational data and enabling sophisticated data-driven inferences, but their hallucination-fluent yet factually incorrect outputs pose significant risks in grid operations. While recent work explores LLM applications through system implementations, theoretical frameworks guiding when and how operators should integrate LLM assistance remain lacking. This paper develops a decision-theoretic framework for human-LLM collaboration, comparing full delegation (automating decisions) versus strategic learning (Bayesian calibration of LLM inferences). We model compound uncertainty from unknown node states and stochastic hallucination errors, deriving closed-form conditions for optimal LLM utilization. Our analysis reveals that full delegation is often suboptimal and may eliminate LLM value entirely. In contrast, strategic learning effectively mitigates hallucination impacts even at high hallucination rates. Moreover, the value of LLM assistance under strategic learning exhibits non-monotonic behavior: though initially declining with hallucination rate, it recovers as operators adaptively discount unreliable outputs. Numerical studies demonstrated that strategic learning significantly outperforms full delegation by up to 200\%. These findings challenge the traditional wisdom of fully delegating to LLM-based agents, demonstrating that human-LLM collaboration through strategic learning is essential for reliable LLM-assisted grid operations.

title: Optimal Monetary Policy Subject to Sovereign Default

detail.title: Optimal Monetary Policy Subject to Sovereign Default
detail.abstract: Public debt has surged in recent years, raising concerns about fiscal sustainability and the risk of sovereign default. This paper's key contribution is to examine optimal monetary policy under those conditions. I develop a New Keynesian model with strategic sovereign default, leveraging a novel solution method. Under standard rule-based monetary policy, inflation rises when default risk increases. A hawkish central bank keeps inflation at target. Under discretion, a positive inflation bias emerges because the central bank has an incentive to "run the economy hot" to erode government debt, failing to account for the inflationary pressure. However, under commitment, the inflation bias is mitigated, enabling the sovereign to borrow more.

detail.abstract: The Pareto criterion defines efficiency as a situation in which no further unanimous improvements remain. Although elegant and widely applied, it evaluates preference stability rather than social welfare. This note clarifies the conceptual difference between efficiency and welfare and argues that meaningful welfare analysis must rely on measurable aggregate gains and losses rather than on individual ordinal preferences.

title: The AI Triad: Power, Infrastructure, and Agency in US-EU-China Strategy

detail.title: The AI Triad: Power, Infrastructure, and Agency in US-EU-China Strategy
detail.abstract: This paper argues that current AI policy debates understate how far the United States, European Union, and China are already constructing a shared but unequal "AI Triad": a tightly coupled system of compute, data, and legal infrastructures that others will have to plug into on largely take-it-or-leave-it terms. Using the AI Matrix (Access × Agency), the Grey Swan scenario lens, and the Orchestrated Intelligence (OI) workflow, we read recent US, EU, and Chinese AI and semiconductor measures as components of a single evolving architecture rather than isolated strategies. A structured corpus of flagship policies is analyzed through AI-assisted OI pipelines with explicit role separation, logging, and human oversight. We show that the Triad is driving Access (compute, capital, infrastructure, regulatory reach) much faster than it is building Agency (skills, institutional capacity, voice) at home or abroad, and that this imbalance shapes the space of plausible futures. Four Grey Swan worlds illustrate how different combinations of Access and Agency redistribute risk across regions and sectors. The paper concludes with concrete levers for governments and firms inside and outside the Triad to raise Agency, using the Triad's own infrastructure without surrendering long-run strategic autonomy.

detail.abstract: Backed by an economic framework offering substantial advantages to operators, Malta’s aircraft registry has experienced significant growth in recent years, with 913 aircraft registered by the end of 2024. This registry supports a diverse range of aviation operations, including commercial airlines, private jet charters, and cargo services, amongst others. This discussion paper provides an in-depth analysis of the Maltese aircraft registry's current profile and constructs a comprehensive dataset of all flights completed by Maltese-flagged aircraft during 2024, subject to some limitations. The analysis reveals that in 2024 alone, Maltese-flagged aircraft conducted 804,000 flights, covering a combined distance of 1,020 million kilometres. These operations consumed approximately 4,554 million kilograms of fuel, releasing 14.39 million metric tons of CO₂ into the atmosphere. As the aviation industry grows in size and complexity, adequate support and resources need to be made available to the respective authorities, in order for Malta to remain at the forefront of global aviation competitiveness.

title: Weaponized AI: A New Era of Threats and How We Can Counter it
affiliations: Mossavar-Rahmani Center for Business and Government, Harvard Kennedy School

detail.title: Weaponized AI: A New Era of Threats and How We Can Counter it
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence has emerged as both a transformative tool and a potential weapon of unprecedented sophistication, presenting serious risks to national security and democratic institutions. Adversarial actors are increasingly exploiting AI's capabilities to destabilize societies, fuel cybercrime, disrupt public order, and undermine democratic institutions. AI's unique combination of scale and accessibility creates unprecedented security challenges that our current governance frameworks are not equipped to address, requiring immediate and comprehensive attention.

title: The Dynamics of Banking Resilience: A Control-Theoretic Approach to Strategic Persistence
affiliations: Universidad del Norte

detail.title: The Dynamics of Banking Resilience: A Control-Theoretic Approach to Strategic Persistence
detail.abstract: This paper develops a novel continuous-time stochastic optimal control model to analyze banking efficiency as a dynamic, path-dependent process. We empirically implement this model using a rich quarterly panel dataset from the Colombian banking sector spanning 2015 to 2023, a period that serves a natural experiment encompassing the regulatory shock of Circular 026 (2017), pronounced macroeconomic shifts, and the unprecedented COVID-19 crisis. This context enables us to disentangle persistent strategic effects from transitory shocks. Employing System GMM estimation, we find that banking efficiency is highly persistent, with gains and losses compounding over time, which indicates significant adjustment frictions and validates the core mechanism of our theoretical framework. Strategic choices, such as aggressive lending, are found to enhance cost efficiency but have negligible effects on other performance metrics, while external shocks influence efficiency in a proxy-specific manner. Our results highlight that resilience in the banking sector derives primarily from consistent long-term strategy rather than episodic intervention. By formally integrating a dynamic theoretical model with empirical evidence from an emerging market, this study provides a new foundation for understanding bank adaptation and resilience.

detail.abstract: Individuals in Malta can take early pensions at 61. The government adopted a deferral scheme, initially for private-sector workers in 2016 and then extended to all by 2019, offering actuarially fair pension increases, made more generous in 2023, and a prohibition of work until pension age for early retirees. Jobsplus data indicate early pension uptake fell from 25% in 2016 to 15% by 2024. During this period exit rates at age 61 fell by 3 points among private sector workers after the scheme’s launch, and when the scheme was extended a large drop occurred among public sector workers. More generous deferral reduced exit rates by between 3 to 5 points across sectors. Overall, the scheme accounts for a quarter of the decline in exit rates, adding 1,800 workers. Replacing this approach with partial pensions for all could reverse these gains; instead, enhancing the current scheme would better support longer careers.

title: GAP-CoT: A Multi-role Multi-path Game-theoretic Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Framework for Industrial Intelligent Decision-making
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: GAP-CoT: A Multi-role Multi-path Game-theoretic Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Framework for Industrial Intelligent Decision-making
detail.abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in language understanding and complex reasoning; however, they still face challenges in high-risk industrial decision-making, such as single-path reasoning, limited knowledge coverage, and poor result robustness. To address these issues, we propose GAP-CoT (Game-theoretic Alliance Path for Chain-of-Thought), a multi-path reasoning framework integrating multi-role modeling and cooperative game-theoretic mechanisms. GAP-CoT constructs an expert alliance using cooperative game theory and a task utility function combining accuracy, domain adaptability, and response efficiency to evaluate role combinations. The Shapley value quantifies each role’s contribution, enabling dynamic selection of optimal coalitions and subtask allocation, simulating real expert collaboration. A dual-loop mechanism generates multiple reasoning paths with multi-perspective causal chains, integrating both domain-specific and general-purpose LLMs. Final outputs are selected and aggregated via a preference scoring scheme and a Nash equilibrium. Using coal mine gas over-limit detection as a case study, GAP-CoT achieved 84.4% average accuracy in a few-shot setting, outperforming standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning by 9.8%, and demonstrated superior performance in causal explanation and recommendation tasks. Cross-model evaluations confirmed its strong generalizability, while ablation studies verified the critical role of multi-role modeling and game-theoretic mechanisms. These results indicate GAP-CoT effectively reconstructs industrial reasoning structures, providing a reliable paradigm for high-risk intelligent decision-making.

title: Too Slow for the AI Age? Building a Dynamic Research Continuum

detail.title: Too Slow for the AI Age? Building a Dynamic Research Continuum
detail.abstract: Academic publishing is misaligned with the tempo of contemporary artificial intelligence. Large models alter capabilities, risks and regulatory questions on a quarterly cycle, while journal review and publication often take years. This tempo gap displaces epistemic authority from public, peerreviewed knowledge to corporate laboratories, private platforms and informal commentary. The paper argues that closing this gap requires redesigning the research pipeline itself. It proposes a Dynamic Research Continuum (DRC): a continuous, versioned publication architecture that integrates preprints, open and AI-assisted review, and "living" synthesis articles into a single visible knowledge loop. Unlike piecemeal open-science reforms, DRC treats access, review and synthesis as one lifecycle explicitly designed for high-velocity AI domains. The architecture is operationalized through the Iterative Human-AI Co-Creation (IHACC) framework, which specifies how human researchers and AI systems cycle through scoping, drafting, critique and updating while preserving judgement, transparency and epistemic inclusion. Using a historical reconstruction of journal publishing, a diagnosis of current challenges in AI-relevant fields and an analysis of reform options, the paper argues that timely, trustworthy and openly updated research has become a precondition for legitimate governance in the AI age.

detail.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive assessment of air quality dynamics across western India, with particular focus on Rajasthan's major urban centers during the COVID-19 lockdown period. Using ground-based observations from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) network and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) reanalysis data, we evaluated pollutant concentrations for PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, and CO across four cities (Jodhpur, Bhiwadi, Jaipur, and Kota) during 2018-2020. The analysis reveals dramatic reductions in pollutant concentrations during lockdown phases, with PM2.5 decreasing by 25-60% and PM10 by 40-75% compared to baseline conditions. Statistical validation demonstrates significantly improved CAMS model performance during 2020, with correlation coefficients increasing substantially and Factor of 2 (FAC2) values exceeding 0.75 for most pollutants. The phase-wise lockdown analysis indicates maximum reductions during Phase 1, with gradual increases in later phases as restrictions relaxed. These findings provide crucial insights into anthropogenic contributions to regional air pollution and demonstrate the potential for substantial air quality improvements through coordinated emission reduction strategies.

title: Financialization of Commodity Markets with Heterogeneous Agents and Supply-Side Information Frictions
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt - Faculty of Economics and Business Administration and

detail.title: Financialization of Commodity Markets with Heterogeneous Agents and Supply-Side Information Frictions
detail.abstract: We develop a general equilibrium model to provide theoretical insights into the interplay among financialization, trader heterogeneity, and market stability in the commodity market. Our model features producers and heterogeneous financial traders, focusing on supply-side information asymmetries and within-trader risk aversion heterogeneity. Producers observe supply-side fundamentals perfectly, while heterogeneous financial traders receive noisy private signals of it. Our findings are threefold. First, expanding total financial trader participation lowers futures price's loading on supply-side fundamentals but raises price informativeness by displacing noise trading, producing non-monotonic volatility, compressing futures risk premium, shifting commodity-equity comovement upward, boosting producers' operating profits while depressing their welfare. Second, increasing the financial hedger's share reduces both supply-side loading and price informativeness, lowers volatility, raises the futures risk premium, and likewise moves the comovement upward, while reducing producers' operating profits but improving their welfare. Third, financial traders' risk aversion heterogeneity and producer-trader and hedger-speculator information asymmetries can amplify or reverse these patterns by shifting the relative weights of speculative and hedging motives.

title: Solving Britain's Housing Crisis: Where and How to Build 1.5 Million Homes
affiliations: University of Warwick and University of Warwick

detail.title: Solving Britain's Housing Crisis: Where and How to Build 1.5 Million Homes
detail.abstract: This paper develops two new hyper-local measures of housing demand—the housing gap and housing tightness—drawing on more than 20 billion housing searches and the full history of listings from Rightmove. We show that excess demand varies far more within Local Authorities than between them, and that new homes have often been built in areas with low demand while high-demand neighbourhoods have been systematically under-served. Using our measures, we identify where new homes should be delivered at the neighbourhood level, finding that around half of Britain’s excess demand can only be met through densification, with the remainder requiring urban extensions, small-town extensions, or new rural developments. We conclude by comparing demand-based housing targets with government targets and offering policy guidance for how to deliver 1.5 million homes in the places where people most want to live.

title: The GENIUS Act and the Quest for Seigniorage
affiliations: Marlowe Capital

detail.title: The GENIUS Act and the Quest for Seigniorage
detail.abstract: This paper explores the macrofinancial and political economy implications of the GENIUS Act, the proposed U.S. framework for the issuance of dollar-backed stablecoins, as part of the emerging contest for monetary dominance in the digital age. It argues that GENIUS effectively deepens the internationalization of the U.S. dollar through private-sector channels. By requiring a 1:1 backing of stablecoins with cash or U.S. Treasuries, the Act creates a mechanism whereby global demand for digital dollars strengthens the USD, increases U.S. borrowing capacity, and generates seigniorage profits for the Treasury. The paper situates this process within the broader evolution of money and a revived Triffin dilemma, from fractional reserve banking to blockchain-based instruments, and contrasts the American approach with the Eurozone’s centralized response through the forthcoming digital euro and the MiCA regulatory framework. It concludes that the GENIUS Act may trigger a new phase of “deep dollarization,” particularly across emerging markets.

title: How Green is Green? Anatomy of ESG Funds' Selection
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: How Green is Green? Anatomy of ESG Funds' Selection
detail.abstract: We examine the stock selection processes of ESG funds and evaluate their effectiveness in delivering meaningful environmental and financial outcomes by comparing them to appropriate benchmarks. ESG portfolios reduce overall emissions by 36%, yet over 90% of this is achieved through strategic elimination of the 2% holdings comprising the top 25 corporate emitters---highlighting a reliance on extensive-margin selection. Active ESG funds employ this approach more aggressively through industry-level exclusions, whereas index ESG funds achieve reductions through stock-level selection within industries. Despite these adjustments, ESG funds maintain holdings closely aligned with their benchmarks, incurring minimal compromises in diversification and systematic risk, and performing on par financially. Notably, ESG index funds outperform both active ESG funds and their non-ESG counterparts. While ESG funds only have modestly higher ESG scores, they demonstrate significantly lower ESG risk exposure. By dissecting the mechanisms underlying ESG portfolio construction, our findings clarify how targeted divestment drives environmental outcomes and why its limited scope constrains broader impact.

detail.title: Public Debt Burden and Crisis Severity

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banco de Espana Working Paper No.2527
