detail.title: Analyzing the Significance of Islamic Marketing in Enhancing Halal Cosmetics Purchase Intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z
detail.abstract: As the countries with the largest Muslim populations, Indonesia and Malaysia can become the center of the world’s largest halal industry. From a study conducted by the researchers in 2024, which compared the intention to buy halal cosmetics of Indonesian and Malaysian Muslim Gen Zs, it was found that the intention to purchase halal cosmetics, with the moderation of each country’s government regulations to use them, was stronger in Malaysian Muslim Gen Z than Indonesian Muslim Gen Z. So this raises the question of whether there are other efforts that the Indonesian government can make to encourage this. Can Islamic Marketing, with its dimensions of Normative, Islamic Ethics and Social Welfare, in the forms of an Environmental sustainability approach and a Humanistic approach, achieve Indonesia’s goal of becoming a global hub for halal cosmetics? The purpose of this research is to analyze the significance of Islamic Marketing in increasing the intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z to purchase halal cosmetics, thereby realizing Indonesia’s commitment in this regard. The unit of analysis in this study is 250 Indonesian Muslim Gen Z individuals residing in the Jabodetabek area of Indonesia, aged 18-28 years, who are also cosmetics users, with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) as the statistical tool. The findings of this study indicate that the influence of Islamic marketing on the intention of Indonesian Muslim Gen Z to purchase halal cosmetics is significantly positive. The social welfare dimension is the strongest influencer of the intention. This intention is further reinforced by the government’s obligation to use such products. The moderating effect of government regulations on their purchase intention outweighs the direct influence of each dimension of Islamic marketing on the intention to purchase. Large halal cosmetics business players in Indonesia can collaborate with the government to make optimal efforts to realize the government’s commitment.

title: The Correlation Between Environmental Concern and Purchase Intention for Eco-Friendly Products Among the Rural Communities in the Philippines
affiliations: Bukidnon State University, Bukidnon State University and Bukidnon State University

detail.title: The Correlation Between Environmental Concern and Purchase Intention for Eco-Friendly Products Among the Rural Communities in the Philippines
detail.abstract: Environmental destruction and global warming are significant global concerns, driving increased public awareness and the need for sustainable consumption. A noticeable gap exists in understanding how global, regional, and local factors influence green purchasing behavior, particularly in rural communities in the Philippines, where the shift from environmental awareness to actual green buying behavior is underexplored. This study aimed to investigate the correlation between environmental concern and purchase intention for eco-friendly products among rural communities, focusing on the influence of ecological awareness on sustainable consumption practices in rural and economically constrained areas. The study employed a descriptive-correlational research design, using survey questionnaires to collect data from residents in the Philippines. The data were analyzed to determine the relationship between environmental concern and purchase intention. Key findings revealed a significant positive correlation between environmental concern and purchase intention for eco-friendly products. While there’s notable environmental awareness, economic constraints and product quality expectations influence the actual purchase of eco-friendly products. The findings emphasize the need for strategies that enhance the transition from environmental concern to purchase intention by addressing affordability, ensuring product quality, and promoting conservation behaviors.

title: Shaping AI Impacts Through Licensing: Illustrative Scenarios for the Design Space

detail.title: Shaping AI Impacts Through Licensing: Illustrative Scenarios for the Design Space
detail.abstract:
Licensing already structures how code, data and models circulate in AI, yet it is rarely treated as a governance instrument. Building on a companion paper that develops six “Commons” logics for impact-oriented AI licensing—Value, Transparency, Sustainability, Access, Reciprocity and Governance—this article turns that design space into concrete scenarios. It shows how clause families could function in practice and spread through procurement, open-source projects, industry consortia and reputational competition.

Licensing is presented as a repeatable, enforceable and system-specific layer within the broader governance landscape. The article addresses issues of measurement, standardisation and interactions with competition, data-protection and sectoral rules, and clarifies its use of “Commons” in the digital-commons tradition: small sets of reusable profiles that accumulate into shared resource layers.

The contribution is to demonstrate that, once licensing is treated as societal infrastructure, concerns about value, transparency, sustainability, access, reciprocity and governance can be translated into tractable clause families for real deployments.

title: Influence of Tiktok Shop Engagement on Skincare Beauty Product Sales in Titok Shop Philippines
affiliations: Independent, Independent and

detail.title: Influence of Tiktok Shop Engagement on Skincare Beauty Product Sales in Titok Shop Philippines
detail.abstract: The growing influence of social commerce platforms has transformed how consumers make purchasing decisions, particularly in the beauty and skincare industry. Despite the rapid rise of TikTok Shop in the Philippines, limited research has explored how its engagement metrics directly affect product sales. Addressing this gap, the research investigated the relationship between TikTok Shop engagement—measured through the number of customer reviews/stars and average product ratings—and the sales performance of skincare beauty products. Using a quantitative descriptive–correlational design, data were gathered from 130 skincare products listed on TikTok Shop between January and March 2025. Descriptive analysis revealed that engagement and sales were highly skewed, with a few viral products dominating consumer attention and purchases. Regression results showed that the number of reviews or stars strongly predicted sales performance, explaining 97.2% of the variance, while average ratings explained only 26.1%. These findings emphasize that the volume of social proof, rather than rating quality, plays a more decisive role in influencing consumer buying behavior in algorithm-driven platforms. The implications suggest that sellers and marketers should focus on strategies that boost customer engagement and review volume to improve visibility and maximize sales potential in social commerce environments.

title: Crafting An Exception to the Principle of Non-Intervention to End Military Coups

detail.title: Crafting An Exception to the Principle of Non-Intervention to End Military Coups
detail.abstract: Oftentimes, when a foreign state refuses to get involved when another country is subjected to a military coup, the foreign state uses the principle of non-intervention as the reason for inaction. The principle of non-intervention in those instances takes on the role of becoming a shield against preserving or protecting human rights. Specifically in Myanmar, the principle of non-intervention is being used as a weapon by the military junta, allowing it to strengthen its grip on the levers of power and crush any fledgling opposition to its rule with unimaginable cruelty and violence. This article advances the premise that a limited exception on utilization of the principle of non-intervention must be recognized in situations where the duly elected government of the people of a State has been displaced by a military junta. Embracing interventions to dislodge a military junta, combined with a refusal by the global community to recognize the military junta as the legitimate government, collectively will serve to weaken the military's coup and lead to their ouster.  The protections envisioned in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights are betrayed by inaction and are essentially meaningless.

title: Sustainable Finance on a Stag Hunt: Addressing Net Zero Coordination Failure in the Asset Management Industry

detail.title: Sustainable Finance on a Stag Hunt: Addressing Net Zero Coordination Failure in the Asset Management Industry
detail.abstract: Net zero commitments continue to challenge the asset management industry. Investors are devoting substantial resources, from time to money to political will, to their targets without attendant changes in the real economy. This paper, offering a novel application of game theory to climate considerations in financial services, models the industry's approach to net zero commitments with a modified stag hunt game. "Stags" here are credible net zero commitments or initiatives that translate into real-world decarbonization, whereas "hares" are lower-risk and shorter-term activities like portfolio reallocations that do not affect global net zero ambitions. Asset owners and asset managers have dramatically different incentives, driven by mismatches in time horizon and views on fiduciary duty. Consequently, hares dominate: a rational but suboptimal status quo. With political pressure against cooperative climate action building, though, an abstention scenario – a poor outcome for climate-motivated investors – is becoming more likely. Incentives can be changed, but until investors are honest with themselves about how they value the climate performance of their portfolio versus of the real economy, they will continue to mistake hares for stags and reject rational hares as negligent.

title: Intersectional or Inseparable? Connecting Theory to Estimands in Studies of Identity
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley, New York University (NYU) - New York University, Abu Dhabi and Harvard University

detail.title: Intersectional or Inseparable? Connecting Theory to Estimands in Studies of Identity
detail.abstract: In studies of inequality and discrimination, researchers often attempt to isolate the relationship between social identities and social outcomes. However, theories of race, class, intersectionality, and racial capitalism suggest that some identities are causally downstream from other identities, or that multiple identities are conceptually intertwined. Focusing on race and class, we investigate what these distinct theories imply for quantitative studies. Specifically, we distinguish five estimands that correspond to different theories about whether race (or class) is developmentally upstream of class (or race), or that race and class are so developmentally intertwined as to be analytically inseparable: 1) a race-first estimand, 2) a class-first estimand, 3) a factorial estimand, 4) an intersectional estimand, and 5) an inseparable estimand. Using three correspondence audit and audit-like experiments in different contexts, we illustrate the empirical importance of distinguishing these estimands when respondents impute information about an individual's class identity from their racial identity.

title: SEC Scrutiny and Corporate Risk-Taking
affiliations: University of Connecticut - Department of Accounting, University of Connecticut and The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: SEC Scrutiny and Corporate Risk-Taking
detail.abstract: We examine whether heightened SEC scrutiny of financial reporting affects corporate risk-taking. Because managers are risk-averse, tightened regulatory oversight could increase risk-taking by strengthening accounting’s governance role, or reduce it by constraining managers’ ability to shield themselves from risky outcomes through earnings management. In 2007, the SEC elevated six district offices to the regional level, expanding their authority and enforcement resources. Using this reorganization in a difference-in-differences design, we find that treatment  firms in the jurisdictions of the newly elevated offices experience declines in idiosyncratic stock return volatility, R&D expenditures, and innovation relative to control firms, consistent with reduced risk-taking. Treatment firms also exhibit lower earnings management. The effects of heightened scrutiny are concentrated among firms where managers face greater career concerns and where earnings management declines most. Overall, our results suggest that increased regulatory scrutiny can dampen corporate risk-taking by constraining managerial reporting discretion and intensifying risk-related agency frictions.

title: Mathematical Principles for Modelling in Finance and Actuarial Science
affiliations: University of Technology, Sydney (UTS) - Finance Discipline Group

detail.title: Mathematical Principles for Modelling in Finance and Actuarial Science

declarations.ethicsApproval: No patients or participants were involved in the research.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received.

detail.abstract: The paper derives the dynamics of an idealized financial market from mathematical principles. It models in market time the dynamics of its basic independent building blocks, the normalized factors, as those of independent stationary scalar diffusions. By assuming the existence of its growth optimal portfolio (GOP) and minimizing the self-information of the stationary joint density of the normalized factors, the security dynamics result. The paper minimizes the divergence of the only practicable pricing measure, the benchmark-neutral pricing measure, from the real-world probability measure. The factors, sums of factors, minimum variance portfolio, factor-GOP, extended market GOP, and stocks turn out to be squared radial Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes that evolve in market time. Additionally, the neutral real interest rate emerges. The derivative of the market time models in market time the average trading intensity, which yields rough volatilities when observed in calendar time.

title: PULSe: Price-Updated Lending Seigniorage A Dynamic K-Percent Rule for Automatic Monetary Stabilisation
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: PULSe: Price-Updated Lending Seigniorage A Dynamic K-Percent Rule for Automatic Monetary Stabilisation
detail.abstract: This paper introduces PULSe (Price-Updated Lending Seigniorage), a rules-based monetary framework that extends Milton Friedman’s k-percent rule using control-system methods. Rather than maintaining a fixed rate of monetary expansion, PULSe adjusts the k-rate dynamically through a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) feedback mechanism that responds to deviations of actual inflation from its target. The system distributes seigniorage through the banking sector as an insurance mechanism: banks receive payments during periods of price stability and make payments during inflationary or deflationary episodes. This aligns private incentives with public price-stability objectives and removes the need for discretionary central-bank intervention. Simulations using historical UK data (1955–2006) show that PULSe would have maintained near-zero average inflation with markedly reduced volatility, while remaining robust to severe measurement noise. The framework offers an automatic, transparent, and self-stabilising alternative to conventional interest-rate policy, bridging economic theory and control engineering.

title: Electronic Filings in EU Company Law and the 28 th Regime Option for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
affiliations: Universite du Luxembourg

detail.title: Electronic Filings in EU Company Law and the 28 th Regime Option for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises

declarations.funderStatement: National Centres of Excellence in Research (NCER) programme, Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR)

detail.abstract: The article evaluates the EU's proposal for a "28th regime" of company law, centred on a European Start-Up and Scale-Up Company (ESSU) and improved electronic filing, and assesses its feasibility amid persistent Single Market fragmentation. Despite SMEs dominating the EU economy, national divergences in incorporation rules, authentication, language, and administration continue to obstruct cross-border growth. The First Digitalisation Directive, aimed at modernising formation through online procedures and interoperable registers, produced uneven and often restrictive national transpositions, as shown by case studies in Germany, Belgium, and Estonia. The article then considers Digitalisation Directive 2.0, which introduces enhanced interoperability, an EU Company Certificate, electronic powers of attorney, and the "once-only" principle, but whose impact depends on Member States' implementation and real-world acceptance of digital documents. Finally, it analyses the ESSU proposal, concluding that meaningful success requires administrative capacity, political commitment, and stakeholder education to avoid repeating past under-realised harmonisation efforts.

title: Contracting for Consumer Trade Compliance
affiliations: University of New Hampshire School of Law (formerly Franklin Pierce Law Center)

detail.title: Contracting for Consumer Trade Compliance
detail.abstract:
Export compliance is becoming increasingly important for parties required to abide by U.S. law, including many online sellers of consumer products. These retailers’ contractual terms with their customers set forth a number of provisions governing the relationship between them, including those which deal with arbitration, indemnification, disclaimer of warranties, and other issues. Many such agreements also purport to create obligations on the part of the consumer as to export control and sanctions compliance relative to the products they purchase. These contract provisions attempt to do so, however, in often markedly different ways, and with language that may leave notable gaps in the breadth of restrictions purportedly created. For example, some such provisions focus primarily on the export of software, even in the case of retailers of physical goods. Some provisions only contain prohibitions against unauthorized exports and leave unaddressed the issue of sanctions compliance. Other versions are far more detailed and specifically prohibit unauthorized transshipments and re-exports, along with other types of prohibited exports.

This Article analyzes the extent to which agreements between online retailers and consumers actually achieve reduced regulatory risk for the companies who use them. First, it compares how these provisions differ among a sample of retailers’ terms of use, and the effect these different provisions have on retailers’ contractual relationships with their customers. The Article also examines the intersection between the private law contractual relationship between retailers and consumers and the public law export controls and sanctions measures to which retailers are subject. Retailers may use these contractual terms to attempt to shield themselves from compliance risk, but the terms at issue are often incomplete and in any case are unlikely to be actually read or understood by consumers. In some cases, they may not even become part of a binding contract between the consumer and the company. This Article suggests more effective ways of drafting these contractual terms, but ultimately concludes that other compliance measures such as IP address monitoring are far more likely to provide a meaningful reduction in compliance risk for retailers.

title: From Clicks to Bricks: The Effect of Economic Nexus Laws on Consumer Spending

detail.title: From Clicks to Bricks: The Effect of Economic Nexus Laws on Consumer Spending

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none at all.
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: Research support provided by the Mays School of Business and Marriott Business School at Texas A&M University and Brigham Young University, respectively.

detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of adopting economic nexus laws on local consumer spending at brick-and-mortar (B&M) retailers. We focus on a natural experiment involving Washington State, which enacted economic nexus in October 2018, and neighboring Oregon, which imposes no sales tax. Utilizing data from the NielsenIQ Consumer Panel survey, we estimate difference-in-differences regressions and find that Washington households increased purchases at B&M retailers relative to Oregon households following adoption. This effect is strongest for taxable goods and in counties near the Washington–Oregon border. We also examine geospatial vehicle data capturing trips from Washington residents to five Oregon shopping centers located along the border. We find a significant increase in trips by Washington residents after the law change, consistent with cross-border sales tax avoidance. Together, the results indicate that the imposition of sales tax on online purchases increases both purchases at B&M retailers and cross-border shopping.

title: How Close Is Close? Spatial Spillover and Boundary Attenuation Effect of Inward FDI On Local Firm Births

detail.title: How Close Is Close? Spatial Spillover and Boundary Attenuation Effect of Inward FDI On Local Firm Births
detail.abstract: This paper enriches the knowledge spillover theory of entrepreneurship, offering further evidence of the spatial spillover and boundary attenuation effect of inward FDI within a local context. Using panel data from 63 Vietnamese provinces during 2016-23, I applies spatial econometrics models and identifies a pattern of entrepreneurial learning and mimicking among adjacent provinces. Inward FDI stimulates local firm births in a given province and externally spillovers to neighbors within 500km, with an elasticity of 0.068 after accounting for spatial dependence. Local socio-economic elements play significant viral agents in the brain drain phenomenon and are mediators in absorbing knowledge to formulate new local firms. The contagion boundaries of economic scaling, labor upgrading, and environmental governing are 350km, 300km, and 100km, respectively. It is worth noting that the knowledge spillover effect has a pattern of attenuation with increasing distance. Thus, the main implication is that policymakers and practitioners should account for spatial interactions to thrive locally if planning to connect globally and establish an entrepreneurial economic circle based on the “center-periphery” structure to resonate the process of knowledge spillover.

title: The ESCB Forecasting Models: What Are They and What Are They Good For?
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB), European Central Bank (ECB), Deutsche Bundesbank and European Central Bank

detail.title: The ESCB Forecasting Models: What Are They and What Are They Good For?

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Occasional Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: This report provides a comprehensive overview of the models and tools used for macroeconomic projections within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB). These include semi-structural models, dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models, time series models and specialised satellite models tailored to particular questions or country-specific aspects. Each type of model has its own strengths and weaknesses and can help answer different questions. The models should therefore be seen as complementary rather than mutually exclusive. Semi-structural models are commonly used to produce baseline projection exercises, since they offer the flexibility to combine expert judgement with empirical data and have enough complexity and structure to provide a good representation of the economy. DSGE models, valued for their internal consistency and strong theoretical foundations, are another core forecasting tool used by some central banks, particularly to analyse counterfactuals. Time series models tend to be better suited to forecasting the short term, while scenario analysis and special events may require satellite models, extensions of existing models or even the development of new models tailored to the question at hand. The report also addresses the challenges to macroeconomic projections posed by data quality, including revisions and missing data, and describes the methods implemented to mitigate their effects. The report identifies “quick wins” to improve the projection process by enhancing the transparency and comparability of results through standardised reporting frameworks and better measurement of the judgement integrated in forecasts. The findings highlight the fundamental role of macroeconomic models in underpinning the ESCB’s projection exercises and ensuring that the Governing Council’s assessments and deliberations rest on coherent, granular and credible analysis of both demand-side and supply-side dynamics.

title: Policy Uncertainty Reduces Green Innovation
affiliations: , NYU Stern School of Business and Singapore Management University - Lee Kong Chian School of Business

detail.title: Policy Uncertainty Reduces Green Innovation
detail.abstract: Policy uncertainty can undermine the power of government subsidies to stimulate environmentally friendly research and development. We show that Chinese firms' green R&D falls as the uncertainty of environmental subsidies rises: Exogenous, weather-driven air pollution variability induces subsidies to fluctuate, and firms in areas with high weather-driven subsidy variability undertake less green R&D and hire fewer technical employees, controlling for the average level of subsidies. Heavy emitters and environmental technology firms are more affected. The results also illustrate how policy uncertainty can arise when policymakers are influenced by conditions that are salient but with causes that are difficult to disentangle.

title: Multi-Agent MBTI-Inspired Cognitive AI for Enhanced Cybersecurity Threat Detection and Analysis
affiliations: Banasthali Vidhyapith, Banasthali, India

detail.title: Multi-Agent MBTI-Inspired Cognitive AI for Enhanced Cybersecurity Threat Detection and Analysis
detail.abstract: We propose a Multi-Agent MBTI-Inspired Cognitive AI framework to enhance intrusion detection systems (IDS) by leveraging cognitive diversity derived from the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI). Each agent, implemented as a RandomForestClassifier with tailored hyperparameters, emulates a unique MBTI profile to capture diverse cyber threat patterns. Evaluated on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, our system achieves up to 90.0% accuracy and 0.902 F1-score, surpassing baseline Random Forest (74.9%) and competing with neural network-based IDS (90.3-91.8%). This work demonstrates the efficacy of cognitive diversity in improving IDS robustness and generalization. We provide a detailed Python implementation, performance analysis, and future directions, including neural network integration and ensemble fusion, to advance next-generation cybersecurity solutions.

title: Adaptive Public Relations in the Digital Disruption Era: A Case Study of PT Pertamina Hulu Indonesia
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Adaptive Public Relations in the Digital Disruption Era: A Case Study of PT Pertamina Hulu Indonesia
detail.abstract: The energy industry plays a crucial role in national economic growth and energy security, yet it faces persistent challenges such as safety issues, environmental impacts, regulatory changes, and increasing public scrutiny that may jeopardize corporate reputation and image. This study examines how Public Relations (PR) functions as a strategic instrument to safeguard reputation in the digital disruption era, focusing on a case study of PT Pertamina Hulu Indonesia (PHI). Using a qualitative methodology, data were collected through an in-depth interview with the company’s Senior Manager Relations and analyzed with reference to adaptive PR concepts including technological transformation, creativity, storytelling, investor relations, and sustainability communication. The findings indicate that PHI has adopted an adaptive PR model that leverages digital platforms, big data, and artificial intelligence, integrates creative engagement programs, employs authentic storytelling, and aligns communication strategies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). These adaptive practices enable the company to maintain credibility, strengthen stakeholder trust, and mitigate reputational risks in a dynamic information environment. The study concludes that corporate reputation in the digital era depends not only on operational achievements but also on consistent, transparent, and data-driven communication strategies. This research contributes to the understanding of adaptive PR practices and provides a benchmark for energy companies and other industries facing similar challenges of digital disruption.

title: The Dynamic Impact of Digital Development on Wages: Evidence from Heterogeneity and Mediation Analysis in China

detail.title: The Dynamic Impact of Digital Development on Wages: Evidence from Heterogeneity and Mediation Analysis in China
detail.abstract: This study investigates the dynamic impact of digital development on provincial wages in China using panel data from 2012 to 2022. Employing a two-step system GMM estimator, our findings reveal several key insights. First, digital development significantly boosts average wages overall. However, this effect is highly heterogeneous. In high-skill and high-income regions, digitalization fosters sustainable, persistent wage growth, reflecting an "empowerment and value-add" model. Conversely, in low-skill and low-income regions, it induces a temporary "shock-andreversal" pattern, with no lasting wage gains. Furthermore, sustainable wage growth is concentrated in the market-oriented private sector, while the effect is transitory in the non-private sector. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that the wage effect is fully mediated through a unified channel of economic transformation toward a knowledgeintensive structure, characterized by the co-evolution of industrial structure upgrading and human capital accumulation. These findings highlight that the wage benefits of digitalization are not automatic but are contingent on regional human capital and institutional environments, offering nuanced policy insights.

title: Predictability of Monetary Policy Surprises and Euro Area Macroeconomic Dynamics
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt - Graduate School of Economics, Finance and Management (GSEFM)

detail.title: Predictability of Monetary Policy Surprises and Euro Area Macroeconomic Dynamics

publicationDetails.detailsText: De Nederlandsche Bank Working Paper No. 850
publicationDetails.journalName: De Nederlandsche Bank Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: I document that high-frequency euro area monetary policy surprises – measured as changes in risk-free rates around the Eurosystem‘s policy announcements – are not exogenous to information regarding macroeconomic news and financial market developments that pre-date the announcements. More specifically, around 20% of the variation of surprises can be explained by pre-dated information. I show that the violation of the exogeneity of conventional surprise measures introduces a considerable bias into estimates on the effects of monetary policy on euro area macroeconomic outcomes.

title: Resource Wealth and Inequality in Pakistan: A Comparative Study of Balochistan and Punjab through the Lens of the Gini Coefficient

detail.title: Resource Wealth and Inequality in Pakistan: A Comparative Study of Balochistan and Punjab through the Lens of the Gini Coefficient
detail.abstract: This paper examines income inequality in Pakistan with a focus on Balochistan and Punjab using the Gini Coefficient. Despite Balochistan's abundance of natural resources such as Reko Diq, Saindak, Sui Gas, and strategic projects like the CPEC, its socioeconomic indicators lag significantly behind Punjab's. The study uses secondary data and a qualitative approach to decompose and analyze income disparities across divisions. Results indicate that resource wealth in Balochistan has not translated into equitable development, primarily due to structural inequality, governance inefficiencies, and uneven infrastructure distribution. detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into regulatory decision-making represents a paradigm shift in how regulatory agencies operate and enforce compliance across industries. This paper examines the current state of AI implementation in regulatory frameworks, analyzes its transformative potential for expediting decision-making processes, and explores future trajectories for AI-enabled regulatory systems. Drawing from an extensive review of academic literature, regulatory guidance documents, and industry implementations, this research demonstrates that AI technologies-including machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics-are fundamentally reshaping regulatory compliance, enforcement, and oversight. The findings reveal that AI can reduce review times by up to 40%, improve accuracy in risk detection, and enable real-time monitoring capabilities that were previously impossible. However, significant challenges remain regarding explainability, algorithmic bias, data quality, and regulatory harmonization. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for responsible AI implementation in regulatory contexts and identifies key areas for future development to ensure that AI serves as an enabler of fair, efficient, and transparent regulatory decision-making.

detail.abstract: Chinese private portfolio equity outflows, though small compared to other Chinese outflows, are growing rapidly because of capital account liberalization and capital flight. Using granular stock-holding data on Qualified Domestic Institutional Investor (QDII) mutual funds, we identify a nascent financial channel of international transmission of Chinese monetary policy to world stocks. Event study analysis around monetary policy announcement days reveals that monetary policy tightening depresses returns of country equity indexes and individual U.S. stocks with QDII fund exposure relative to non-exposed stocks. The results are robust to controlling for the real transmission channel of Chinese monetary policy and other confounders. The effect is driven by smaller and less liquid firms, but not by China-concept stocks or those highly exposed to China’s macroeconomic shocks. We also find that the results are driven by household portfolio rebalancing from more to less risky assets following the announcement.

detail.abstract: Sari-sari stores serve as vital pillars of rural economies in Northern Mindanao, providing essential goods, local employment, and fostering social cohesion within communities. Despite their significance, many of these microenterprises face enduring challenges, including limited access to capital, weak financial management, and competition from larger retail chains. Ensuring their sustainability is therefore crucial for supporting inclusive rural development. However, limited empirical research has examined localized strategies that promote the long-term growth of these stores across rural Mindanao, creating a notable research gap. This paper explores the demographic characteristics and sustainable growth strategies of sari-sari store owners in rural locality in Northern Mindanao focusing on financial performance, customer retention, and community engagement. A quantitative descriptive design was employed, surveying store owners through a structured questionnaire and analyzing data using descriptive statistics such as frequency, percentage, and mean. Findings indicate that store ownership is predominantly female and concentrated among older adults who exhibit strong financial discipline, community ties, and customer-oriented service. Nonetheless, challenges remain in innovation, income disparity, and cautiousness in offering credit. The results underscore the importance of capacity-building initiatives, financial literacy programs, and youth entrepreneurship engagement to enhance resilience and competitiveness. These insights contribute to the formulation of policies supporting financial inclusion and sustainable rural enterprise development in Northern Mindanao.

detail.abstract: Macroeconomic stability has returned to Ghana following the 2021 economic crisis, yet its benefits remain unevenly distributed. This paper examines the disconnect between macroeconomic indicators and lived experiences, particularly within Ghana's informal sector. It draws on qualitative observations, official data and institutional analysis, and argues that while stabilisation under the ongoing IMF program has helped to restore fiscal balance and currency strength, the resulting growth has been largely extractive rather than inclusive. detail.abstract: Financial cycles refer to fluctuations in credit and house prices that extend beyond typical business cycles. Despite its significance for both monetary and macroprudential policy, the question of how monetary policy shapes financial cycles remains largely unanswered. We extract innovations from a vector autoregression that account for most of the cyclical co-movement between credit and house price growth at medium frequencies. Our findings indicate that systematic monetary policy plays a crucial role in propagating this innovation and can significantly dampen financial cycles, particularly when counteracting house price movements. These stabilizing effects could have substantially mitigated the U.S. financial cycle during the 2000s.

title: Erotic AI and the Erosion of Safety Standards: A Competitive Analysis of Boundary Management in Large Language Models

detail.title: Erotic AI and the Erosion of Safety Standards: A Competitive Analysis of Boundary Management in Large Language Models
detail.abstract:
This paper examines erotic interactions with large language models (LLMs) not as a content-moderation anomaly but as a revealing case of market-driven governance erosion. In October 2025, OpenAI announced the introduction of erotic functionalities for verified adults, prompting public debate framed largely as a moral question of whether AI should produce sexual content. We argue this framing obscures the structural dynamic at stake: the privatization of ethical boundary-setting and the emergence of a competitive logic in which firms justify safety reductions by referencing rivals' behavior.

Drawing on the Centre for the Governance of AI's framework of "risk relative to competitors," we show how a single boundary-crossing actor can normalize erosion across the ecosystem. To empirically ground this claim, we conducted an exploratory probe: a standardized sexually explicit prompt was administered to six major LLMs (Grok, ChatGPT, Gemini, Meta AI, Claude, Perplexity), and their first-turn responses were analyzed. Results reveal three strategic patterns: rupture (explicit acceptance), managed degradation (non-explicit erotic reframing), and restrictive elasticity (categorical refusals with future-flexibility cues). These patterns align with corporate positioning rather than technical capability.

We argue that erotic AI constitutes a frontier of behavioral and affective data extraction, amplified by identity-linking age-verification requirements. The central governance risk is not the production of sexual content itself but the construction of identity-desire datasets, the potential for emotional manipulation, and the normalization of intimacy as a product affordance. Erotic AI thus exposes a wider shift: boundaries of acceptable risk and intimacy are increasingly defined by competitive dynamics, not democratic deliberation.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates when monetary policy announcements matter for asset price dynamics. We identify a fundamental heterogeneity in FOMC statements based on the underlying nature of information conveyed about future policy. Using a simple but novel classification, we identify meetings that convey substantial information about uncertainty surrounding future policy. These statements-one-third of the total-drive most, if not all, of the effects of monetary policy on longterm interest rates and account for a large fraction of their variation on these days. In contrast, directional statements about the policy stance-half of all meetings-have no effect on long-term rates but do affect short-term rates and stock prices. The strong effects on long-term rates stem from term premium adjustments rather than expected future short-term rates, consistent with investors' updating their assessment of higher-order moments of future policy developments. Our classification resolves why policy announcements explain little variance in long-term rates despite driving their dynamics over time.

detail.abstract: This academic article analyzes the relationship between higher education and the labor market in Costa Rica faces significant challenges, particularly regarding the employability of university graduates. This study analyzes how the competencies developed in Costa Rican universities align with the demands of a constantly evolving labor market, characterized by digitalization and globalization. Key gaps are identified, such as the oversupply of professionals in saturated fields and the lack of technical and transversal skills in strategic disciplines, especially in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). The analysis also addresses factors that hinder labor market integration, such as the lack of practical experience and the disconnect between higher education institutions and the productive sector. Key actions are proposed, including curriculum updates, the strengthening of internship programs, and the incorporation of technologies into educational processes. Furthermore, the importance of effective coordination among universities, government, and the productive sector is emphasized to reduce employability gaps, strengthen the national human capital, and ensure sustainable development that meets the demands of the contemporary labor market.

detail.abstract: While Artificial Intelligence (AI) delivers impressive results in the consumer domain, its integration into business is marked by widespread failure. This paper argues that this paradox stems from a fundamental misconception of the critical role of information within business workflows. To address this, we introduce a formal "small world model" of the firm as a decision space to explain how AI usage can fundamentally alter outcomes at the process level. We model the firm via Stocks (resources) and Flows (transformations), governed by the IDEA operator (Information → Decision → Action). Within this rigorous framework, AI's sole function is defined as providing a marginal improvement in information quality or latency (∆Information) for decisions at Critical Election Points (CREPs) within workflows. This allows us to trace precisely how AI creates leverage: by enhancing the expected utility of specific, high-sensitivity decisions. The model yields five formal propositions detailing these mechanisms. This small world model is the foundation for the pragmatic CROP Framework, a diagnostic tool for identifying and exploiting leverage points in real workflows. Offering a micro-founded, information-centric perspective, this paper provides a basis for understanding, diagnosing, and leveraging AI's business impact, moving towards effective AI Business Integration.

title: One Step Forward, Two Steps Back: The EU and the Western Balkans After the Adoption of the New Enlargement Methodology and the Conclusions of the Zagreb Summit

detail.title: One Step Forward, Two Steps Back: The EU and the Western Balkans After the Adoption of the New Enlargement Methodology and the Conclusions of the Zagreb Summit
detail.abstract: Montenegro and Serbia are stuck in the EU accession negotiations, while, with Albania and North Macedonia, the perspective of their future course is very unclear. Between still relatively fluid elements of the new enlargement methodology presented in February 2020, and quite a weak political impulse given by the Zagreb Declaration adopted in May 2020, the potential accession to the EU of the four Western Balkans candidate countries remains not only uncertain, but seems even less realistic than it was after the Thessaloniki Summit in 2003. The paper shows how, just in the first five months of 2020, the path of the Western Balkans towards EU accession has managed to go one timid step forward and two solid steps back. First, some elements of a novel approach to accession are encouraging, but remain imprecise, often inapplicable and subject to potential divergent interpretation. Second, maintained top-down conditionality, combined with internal difficulties of all Western Balkans countries and their high adjustment costs to meet membership criteria could lead to the crumbling of pro-European consensus and a decline of democracy. Finally, the Conclusions of the Zagreb Summit mentioned neither accession nor membership in the EU, confirming the wavering political support for enlargement among Member States. The main methods used in the paper are content analysis and the comparative legal method, while the analysis of the Montenegrin and Serbian case provides evidence for the correlation between the weaknesses of the Zagreb Declaration and the hypothesised second step back in the accession process.

detail.abstract: Poliomyelitis remains a persistent global health threat, particularly in low-resource settings where fragmented data collection and reporting systems undermine surveillance effectiveness. In Ethiopia, existing surveillance tools like District Health Information Software 2 and Global Polio Eradication Initiative lack the granularity, interoperability, and real-time capabilities necessary for effective Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP) data repository. As part of alleviating this challenge, this study presents the development of an AFP surveillance data repository tailored to Ethiopia's context by integrating mobile data collection through our recently developed PolioAntenna App, health system data from Ethiopian Public Health Institute, community data from CORE Group and community engagement as a main data sources. The data repository addresses data fragmentation by enabling structured data capture, real-time analysis, metadata management, policy suggestion, and localized decision-making through an interactive dashboard. This work utilizes a robust data repository framework to facilitate the acquisition, integration, storage, disaggregation, and use of data for advanced analytics and public access. The collected from diverse sources processed through Extract, Transform, Load tools to ensure seamless transformation and loading into a centralized data warehouse. The system supports both real-time and batch data ingestion, orchestrated by tools such as Apache Airflow. Once in the warehouse, data is disaggregated, then organized into dedicated data marts for specific use cases. These marts support downstream applications including data science via Jupyter notebooks, real-time dashboards, machine learning services, and open data portals. The architecture ensures data quality, privacy, and governance, while enabling high-throughput analytics and public accessibility through structured metadata and cataloging systems. Sample results from the system demonstrate improved data completeness, early outbreak detection, and regional case distribution analysis. The data repository serves as a critical asset for researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders by providing timely, disaggregated, and high-quality data to guide evidence-based decisions. It enhances the capacity to detect outbreaks early, monitor immunization efforts, and evaluate intervention outcomes. By centralizing and standardizing diverse data sources, the platform supports cross-sector collaboration, accelerates digital health transformation, and strengthens disease surveillance systems in resource-limited settings.

detail.abstract: Using anonymized consumer credit bureau data, I examine the credit market consequences of student loan delinquency and default and the role that student loan servicers play in contributing to borrower outcomes. I exploit random assignment of student loan borrowers to student loan servicers of varying quality to study the direct effect of servicers on borrowers’ credit outcomes and to isolate variation in the likelihood of default that is not correlated with borrower characteristics. I find that being assigned to a higher-default servicer increases a borrower’s likelihood of default by approximately 6%. However, there is a precisely estimated null effect of servicer assignment on measures of borrowers’ likelihood of financial distress, credit access, and zip code characteristics. These findings suggest that averting a servicer-induced default does not yield considerable benefits for marginal borrowers’ credit outcomes but that servicers are meaningful drivers of student loan repayment outcomes.
